Potato___Early_blight.advice: Remove affected lower leaves and dispose of infected plant debris safely. Water at the base of the plant, apply mulch to reduce soil splash, improve spacing and airflow, and rotate crops. If the disease continues to spread, consult a local agricultural expert about an approved fungicide for potatoes.

Potato___Late_blight.advice: Treat this as a potentially urgent disease because late blight can spread rapidly in cool, wet conditions. Avoid overhead irrigation and handling wet plants. Isolate and safely remove severely affected plants, inspect nearby plants, and contact a local agricultural expert promptly. Use only a locally approved potato fungicide according to its label.

Potato___healthy.advice: No disease detected by the image model. Continue regular inspections, maintain well-drained soil, water appropriately, provide balanced crop nutrition, and monitor leaves and stems for new symptoms.

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.advice: Remove affected leaves when practical and dispose of infected material safely. Avoid overhead watering and working among wet plants. Clean and disinfect tools, use disease-free seeds or seedlings, and rotate crops. If symptoms spread, seek local agricultural advice before selecting a suitable treatment.

Tomato___Early_blight.advice: Remove affected lower leaves without removing more than one-third of the foliage at once. Mulch the soil, water at the base, improve airflow, and remove infected crop debris. Rotate away from tomatoes and related crops for at least two years where practical. Consider a locally approved fungicide if disease pressure warrants it.

Tomato___Late_blight.advice: Act promptly because late blight can spread quickly under cool, wet conditions. Inspect nearby plants, avoid wetting foliage, and safely remove severely affected plants. Obtain prompt confirmation from an agricultural expert and use only an approved tomato treatment according to its label. Observe the required pre-harvest interval.

Tomato___Leaf_Mold.advice: Reduce humidity and prolonged leaf wetness, particularly in greenhouses. Increase ventilation, space and prune plants appropriately, and water at the base. Remove infected leaves and clean tools and growing structures. If the disease persists, seek advice on a suitable locally approved fungicide.

Tomato___Mosaic_virus.advice: There is no curative spray for tomato mosaic virus. Isolate suspected plants and seek confirmation if symptoms are uncertain. Remove confirmed infected plants safely, disinfect tools and wash hands, avoid tobacco contamination during handling, and use resistant varieties and clean planting material in future crops.

Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.advice: Remove affected lower leaves and dispose of infected plant material safely. Avoid overhead watering, mulch the soil to limit splash, provide good airflow, and disinfect tools after handling diseased plants. Rotate crops and consider a locally approved fungicide if the disease continues to spread.

Tomato___Spider_mites.advice: Inspect the undersides of leaves for tiny mites, stippling, and fine webbing. Reduce plant water stress and dust, and use a gentle water spray on leaf undersides when appropriate. Preserve beneficial predatory insects. If infestation is severe, choose a locally approved miticide or insecticidal soap and follow its label.

Tomato___Target_Spot.advice: Remove affected leaves and crop debris, avoid overhead irrigation, improve plant spacing and airflow, and avoid working among wet plants. Because target spot can resemble other leaf-spot diseases, confirm the diagnosis before selecting a fungicide. Rotate approved fungicide groups when advised by a local crop-protection expert.

Tomato___Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.advice: There is no curative treatment for tomato yellow leaf curl virus. Inspect plants for whiteflies, remove confirmed infected plants according to local agricultural guidance, control weeds that may host pests, and use resistant varieties and healthy seedlings. Monitor whiteflies with suitable traps and use locally approved, integrated pest-management methods.

Tomato___healthy.advice: No disease detected by the image model. Continue regular inspections, maintain well-drained soil, water appropriately, provide balanced crop nutrition, and monitor leaves and stems for new symptoms.
